# BDD Harness

**The registry drives the suite, and the tests are committed artefacts of it.** `docs/scenarios.yaml` says what the engine must do; `build tests` renders one Go test per scenario into the file its `path:` names; `pkg/testkit/bddgo` runs it. No feature files. A scenario with an unbound step FAILS — never skipped, never silently absent. See `docs/scenarios.yaml` for the scenario shape (real examples, E2E-001 onward).

**Every test file under `tests/*/` beginning `// Code generated` is written by `true-bdd build tests --fix` and nothing else** — deterministic codegen: the same registry always renders the same bytes, which is what lets `build tests` verify by regenerate-and-compare. A stale file is a startup refusal naming the regeneration command. The AI turn survives only where judgement is needed: authoring step definitions.

Generated tests state their steps literally, and `Done()` compares them against the registry entry before running any — a disagreement stops the scenario with both sides printed. The registry supplies what is not behaviour: description, `service:`, `timeout:`.

**`path:` is required on every scenario, never defaulted.** Several scenarios may share one file (emitted in id order — grouping is editorial). The generator refuses a `path:` outside `tests/<service>/` — the mirror of `services/<service>/`, and the directory it derives the package clause and scenarios import from — one not ending `_test.go`, one inside `steps/`, and two ids rendering one Go name. A path shared across services is now unreachable rather than refused: the directory decides the service (ADR 0009).

**Hand-written guards** (`tests/*/coverage_test.go`) keep the generated set honest — hand-written so the generator cannot silence them by regenerating: `TestScenarioCoverage` (every scenario ↔ exactly one generated test, in the named file), `TestStepCoverage` (every step binds to exactly one definition), `TestFixtureTreesArePaired` (bdd-cli only — bdd-web drives no fixture trees). None brings a harness up; all answer in under a second. bddgo's own refusals: a service the architecture does not declare, a step matched by two definitions, a generated test naming a scenario the registry no longer holds, a `Done()` never called.

**Step prefixes** — two hand a step to a model, each legal in exactly one block; the wrong block is a refusal, not a reinterpretation:

| prefix | legal in | means | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm:` | given/when | a model performs the step, one agent turn at its position | `bddgo.Actor` |
| `judge:` | then | a model rules on the clause — collected, then ONE call after every other step passed | `bddgo.Judgeable` |

Use `judge:` only for what no comparison can settle (two wordings meaning the same thing). The bdd-cli state implements only `Judgeable`; neither suite implements `Actor` yet — deliberate forward work for the web scenarios.

**Fixtures**: each bdd-cli scenario drives a tree at `tests/bdd-cli/fixtures/<name>/` — `input/` (the designed host-project content) and `cassettes/` (one dir per AI call plus `golden.json`). **There is no manifest** — what the run does comes from the scenario; its Given step names the tree. A tree no scenario names fails the whole run. Three optional files at the fixture ROOT, read **by content** rather than executed by path: `prep.sh` (runs after the input overlay, before the pre-run snapshot; non-zero aborts), `teardown.sh` (at SCENARIO end — after both snapshots AND after every Then step, whatever the verdict; never masks it. Late deliberately: a Then step that re-runs the host suite needs the stack the run left standing), `checklist-prompts.yaml` (narrows the checklist walk, keyed by stem; present-but-empty is refused). The scenario still names all three as Given steps; the step definitions verify the tree establishes them.

**Record/replay**: `pkg/testkit/aiproxy` is one binary installed as `claude`/`crush`/`codex` in a shim dir prepended to the subprocess PATH — **one dir per CALLER**, because the shim reads its whole configuration from flat env vars, so separate dirs are the only way the engine can replay while the judge records. A recording shim skips EVERY dir in `TRUE_BDD_AIPROXY_KNOWN_SHIMS` when hunting the genuine CLI, not just its own: with two shims on PATH, skipping only its own finds the other and execs it, which recurses. A `live` caller actively SCRUBS the other caller's shim dir and the four `TRUE_BDD_AIPROXY_*` vars from the spawn it controls — inheritance is the default, and a caller that keeps another's shim has its turns answered from the wrong shelf, consuming that shelf's cursor on the way. A cassette stores argv, stdin, output streams, exit code, and fs-diff, with volatile paths normalized (`{{CWD}}`, `{{RUN_DIR}}`, `{{HOME}}`) in paths, contents AND stdout. Replay matches by sequence per binary, verifies a request hash — mismatch = loud "stale cassette" failure, **exit 86**, never a silent fall-through — applies the fs-diff, and lingers until the engine closes stdin. **Cassettes are sanitized before writing** (the agent CLI's system/init inventory dropped, home rewritten); `scripts/commit`'s recording sweep re-checks committed recordings — a hit means fix the shim and re-record, **never hand-edit a cassette**.

**Grading, three levels, each owning what the others cannot say**: (1) the scenario's Then steps — every mechanical assertion (exit code, stdout, file diff, AI-turn counts) **and any suite the scenario re-runs itself**, every mode; (2) the recording, replay only — `golden.json` byte-compare, every cassette consumed (`runner.CheckCassettesConsumed`), request hash per call; (3) the judge — the `judge:` clauses, **every mode**, one verdict per clause as schema-enforced JSON (`--json-schema`) on the pinned `engine.models.quick` model, in a tool-less headless turn through `pkg/cli/claude`; a malformed reply is an infrastructure error, never a scenario verdict. Under `tests:replay` that verdict is SERVED BACK from the fixture's own judge shelf rather than re-ruled, and a replayed verdict is not billed — the cassette carries the cost the recording spent once, and charging it again would report money no run spent. A fixture asked to replay a verdict it never recorded fails THAT fixture at its Given step, naming the command that records it; that failure is infrastructure, never `ErrJudgeRefused`, or `grade()`'s suppression would hide the golden mismatch beside it. **Cassettes belong to the When stage; Then is the same code path in every mode.** Levels 2 and 3 do not overlap and neither discharges the other: the golden and the census are WHEN-fidelity (the replay reproduced the recorded tree and consumed every turn), the judge grades the outcome's semantics, and both must hold. The judge prompt is generated by `runner.buildJudgeUserPrompt` — clauses rendered under a scope paragraph and one shared `## Tolerances` policy; nothing else feeds it. Noise dirs (`.git`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`) are excluded from both snapshots; `tmp/` is excluded from the judge's diff outright (`runner.judgeGraded`) — the goldens already ignore it, no clause names it, and it carries the agent CLIs' own scratch, a 128KB SQLite db among it. The judge's diff is otherwise WHOLE: no per-file or total byte cap, since trimming it is what failed E2E-042 on content it was never shown. **The judge is measurable under `services:replay,tests:live`**, and that is why that pairing exists: `JudgeRequest` is `(Cmd, Clauses, Diff)` and nothing else, and a green golden certifies that input is byte-identical run to run — so `judge_input_hash` (sha256 of the rendered user prompt, in `harness.json`) equal across two runs with different verdicts is the judge's own noise, and a differing hash is harness drift. A series is N separate `go test` invocations, never `-count=N`: `bootOnce` shares one session root and `prepareRunDir` wipes the fixture dir each iteration, leaving one surviving data point. Residual gap, stated plainly: a change touching only `tmp/` scratch and neither stdout nor an output file is not caught.

**Step-text conventions**: `and:`/`but:` are display-only sugar, interchangeable and unlimited (keyword excluded from the match text; convention: `but:` for a group's negative clause). Two path-argument families: the story steps (`the story "…"`, `… of the story "…"`) take a **glob that must resolve to exactly one file** — zero and two matches each fail; the diff/content steps (`the file "…" is created/modified/unchanged/matches`, `has exactly N lines`) take a **literal path**. Where a created file's name is unknowable: `exactly N file(s) matching "<glob>" is created`. Stdout patterns and regex tails run undelimited to end of line — several carry double quotes of their own. **`the command "<argv>" run in "<dir>" exits with code N`** re-runs a suite the scenario names, in a directory under the run's tmpdir, through `pkg/cli/spec` — the outcome check that a `build code` scenario means: the tests the fix loop was driving actually pass. Put it LAST among the mechanical Thens, since a re-run may append to files earlier clauses count (E2E-005's `suite-runs.log`), and prefer it over file-existence proxies — E2E-011 once failed a correct product over an optional `next.config.*` while its browser assertion was green.

**Tmpdir assembly**: repo layer first (tracked `true-bdd/` + `templates/`, so fixtures exercise the live templates), then the fixture's `input/` overlaid on top — fixture files win, so a fixture may ship a variant checklist or config. Snapshot after prep, before the run: the graded diff holds only what the run itself changed.

**go.mod sentinels, two traps**: (1) a fixture input tree carrying `.go` files must carry a sentinel `go.mod` — run dirs live inside the repo module, and without a boundary the root `go test ./...`/lint compile the deliberately-failing tests past runs left there; (2) `tests/bdd-cli/fixtures/go.mod` covers cassette `fsdiff/after/` trees, which record only what an AI turn *changed* and so carry no `go.mod` of their own. That sentinel is never materialised into a run dir (the runner overlays `<fixture>/input/`, not the fixture directory).

**Modes and gates**: a `//go:build bdd` tag hides the suite from default `go test ./...`. One scenario = one top-level test named after its id (`TestE2E016`), so `-run` names a scenario. `-mode` names a mode per CALLER — `services:` the engine under test, `tests:` the harness's own judge — and both are always named: there is no shorthand and no default, since a mode nobody typed is how a run bills real money believing it replays. An ABSENT `-mode` stays legal and is refused at `bootHarness`, not at the flag: the coverage guards pass none and bring no harness up. `requiredCLIs` gates per axis — a replaying services caller needs no CLI at all, and only a non-replaying `tests:` axis needs `claude`. Live/record skip per scenario when a needed CLI is missing; **replay skips for nothing**. **`services:replay,tests:replay` is back ON the gate**: it reaches no model, needs no key, costs nothing and runs the whole suite in under a minute (`scripts/gates/table.go`). One gate list, one runner: `ci.yml` calls `go run ./scripts/cmd/gates run` and names no gate of its own (`gates.TestCIDoesNotHandListGates` pins that). Gate failure kinds: exit 86 = stale cassette, re-record the affected fixtures; golden mismatch = the run produced different files than the recording — the regression signal, worth reading before re-recording. bdd-web runs only its `TestScenarioCoverage` guard in the gates; `TestStepCoverage` joins when the web step definitions land (~1680 unbound steps across 243 ported scenarios today — tracked at <https://app.clickup.com/t/86cb6fjwy>). The same arithmetic is why `build tests` on this repo does not yet cost zero AI turns.

**A scenario's CLI run is capped at 5 minutes unless its registry entry declares `timeout:`** (`scenarios.scenarioTimeout`). A walk over a multi-prompt checklist blows past that — E2E-292's eight cells take about seven minutes — and the kill surfaces at the When step as `command timed out after 5m0s` (`shell.ErrTimeout`), the partial recording discarded. **Size the budget from the turn count** — the fixture's cassette-dir count is that number. Measured over a full record run (126 turns, 2026-08-30) a turn costs 53s with a 53s standard deviation, so `N x 53s + 3σ√N + 2m` rounded up to five minutes gives 15m at 5 turns, 20m at 7-10, 25m at 12. A cap that merely covers the expected total is a coin flip: E2E-042's twelve turns average about ten minutes against the 10m it used to declare, and it timed out.

`--fix` scenarios supply keystrokes via `the <role> answers "1" to every prompt` — a generous run of that answer, one line per prompt; surplus lines are harmless (EOF exits the CLI cleanly).

**Known, deliberate inconsistency:** the `us-refine-*` fixtures still ship the OLD `quality_gate.tests.{integration,e2e}` architecture shape, and the `us-refine` checklist still cites "the framework per service and per layer". Nothing parses those documents, so the cassettes stay valid — but do not read those fixtures as the current spec shape. Why it is deferred, what to change and how to verify: `docs/for_further/us-refine-fixture-respec.md`.

**Run dirs** — `tmp/test_run/<timestamp>/<fixture>/`: predictable, never auto-cleaned. `bdd-cli-logs/` are recorder sidecars written from `t.Cleanup` (after both snapshots, never in the judge's diff): `harness.json` (verdict, cost, `judge_input_hash`; its presence means the fixture is final — the report server's cache key), `judge-{system,user,response}.txt`, `manifest.json` (what the run was held to as it resolved it). `tmp/true-bdd.log.json` is the engine's own slog, written during the run. At the session root: `session.json` (the `-mode` and planned fixtures, written before the first fixture), `harness.log.json` (the test process's slog), `.cassettes-staging/<fixture>/` (record-mode cassettes + golden, promoted into `fixtures/` only when the fixture passes; the judge's shelf stages at `<fixture>/judge/` inside it, so a run recording both publishes them in one rename, and a run recording only the judge merges that one directory rather than replacing the cassettes it replayed from).
